video.title: This AI Finds the Idea, Customers, and Does the Work

summary: Chris Koerner interviews Alex from Hyper Agent (built by Airtable), a platform for persistent, named AI agents that browse the web, spin up sub-agents and run on schedules ('live mode'). Demos include an agent that finds local businesses with great reviews but no or poor websites and builds them new sites, an always-on 'Signal' outbound sales agent that builds personalised landing pages per prospect, a pond-dredging lead database proof of concept, and a Facebook Marketplace scout. Chris then uses Hyper Agent to research boring $500k businesses, builds a laundromat opportunity map and saves it as a daily 'Deal Scout' agent. Key takeaway: treat agents as 24/7 employees with narrow permissions, and use them for lead generation, personalised outreach and agency delivery; the content is largely a product demo with promotional bias.

ideas.name: Agent-built websites for local businesses with great reviews but no website
ideas.one_liner: An AI agent finds well-reviewed local businesses with no or outdated websites, builds a bespoke site for each, and drafts outreach offering to sell or give it away.
ideas.business_model: One-off website build fees (or free site as a lead-in to paid services)
ideas.customer: Local small businesses (e.g. auto shops) with 300+ Google reviews but no or outdated website
ideas.problem: Great local businesses are hard to find online because they lack a modern website
ideas.offer: A ready-made, business-specific website with booking and estimate features, stood up within days; possibly given free as a hook

pricing.model: Per-site implementation fee, or free giveaway as lead magnet
pricing.notes: No prices stated; example site's estimate pricing was just agent best-guess

acquisition_channels.details: Agent finds contact info, drafts per-business outreach from the user's email; user can approve or let the agent send. Old manual approach was said to get 0.5-1% response.

quote.text: Your response rate is going to be 0.5%, 1% maybe.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

acquisition_channels.details: Candidates sourced by finding businesses with strong Google reviews but weak or no web presence

ideas.delivery: Agent researches the brand and customer reviews, then builds the website (with booking system and estimate tool) in roughly 20-30 minutes for a batch; a human would customise it to the specific business once the deal is won.
unit_economics_claims: Whole run (research to multiple built sites) took about 20-30 minutes
ideas.startup_cost: Free skill on the Hyper Agent marketplace; platform credits needed

acquisition.how: Agent finds prospects and drafts emails, but UK PECR bars unsolicited email to sole traders/individuals; only limited companies are legal targets, so heavy filtering and human approval needed.

onboarding.how: Agent can reply to inbound responses, collect requirements and tailor the site; human confirms scope.

delivery.how: Agent generates the site from reviews and brand research; human spot checks and domain/hosting setup.

billing.how: Invoices and payment links can be automated with standard tools.

support.how: Inbox agent handles routine queries; edits and issues need occasional human input.

uk_applicability.notes: Works in the UK via Google reviews; outreach must respect PECR (cold email to limited companies only, no unsolicited messages to sole traders). Many UK micro-businesses are sole traders, shrinking the legal target pool.

risks: PECR restricts cold outreach to sole traders
Building sites unsolicited may be low-converting
AI sites need customisation and quality checks

quotes.text: Your agent can go and find these candidates and actually build them new digital properties to the point where you could sell the implementation of that website specific to them.
quotes.speaker: Alex

quotes.text: Or there's even this notion that maybe that website is just like a free giveaway because of just how easy it is and how fast it is to do this at scale.
quotes.speaker: Alex

ideas.name: Always-on outbound sales agent with personalised landing pages (Signal)
ideas.one_liner: A persistent agent finds prospects matching an ICP, researches each, builds a personalised landing page/video proposal, handles replies and CRM, and reports to Slack hourly.
ideas.business_model: Platform subscription/credits for the user; the underlying use is B2B lead generation
ideas.customer: B2B companies selling high-consideration products (example: Swiss Solar selling self-cleaning solar panel tech to industrial solar project leads)
ideas.problem: Cold emails get ignored; buyers say 'send me materials'; slow follow-up loses warm leads
ideas.offer: Hyper-personalised proposal pages (hero video, screenshots, explainers) for each prospect, with a CTA to book a study or pilot

pricing.notes: Hyper Agent pricing not given; free initial credits via link

acquisition_channels.details: Personalised outreach linking to a bespoke landing page per project lead, plus overnight inbox agent replying to inbound and replies

quote.text: we think we have a much better chance getting uh someone on the on the phone after receiving a proposal like that than just a plain uh text kind of cold email.
quote.speaker: Alex

acquisition_channels.details: Agents also run ads end to end: creative strategy, spend optimisation, scaling winners and killing losers

ideas.delivery: Agent runs in 'live mode', re-running its self-written prompt hourly: sources prospects, deep research, builds pages and videos, updates CRM, posts to Slack, and learns which messaging gets replies.
ideas.startup_cost: not stated; free credits offered via link

acquisition.how: Agent sources and personalises at scale; UK PECR limits cold email to limited companies and needs human approval/screening.

onboarding.how: Inbox agent responds immediately and books calls.

delivery.how: Pages, videos and research generated by agents.

billing.how: Depends on the seller's own process; not covered.

support.how: Agent handles replies; humans take sales calls.

uk_applicability.notes: Technique is location-agnostic; apply PECR and GDPR to prospect data.

risks: Platform vendor demo with no conversion numbers

quotes.text: The most popular agent on our marketplace... is called Signal. This is your always on 247 sales agent.
quotes.speaker: Alex

ideas.name: AI visual proposals for inbound leads (landscaping, paving, apparel)
ideas.one_liner: Agents reply instantly to inbound leads with AI-generated visuals of the proposed work, such as a redesigned yard, repaved lot or branded apparel.
ideas.business_model: Per-job sales for service companies, enhanced by agent-generated proposals
ideas.customer: Landscaping, commercial paving and corporate apparel companies and their customers
ideas.problem: Competitors take days to respond and customers cannot visualise the result
ideas.offer: Instant reply with a visual of the finished result and rough estimate

acquisition_channels.details: Inbound leads answered immediately; paving firm uses satellite imagery plus AI image generation with cost estimates; apparel firm puts a prospect's branding on products

ideas.delivery: Physical work (landscaping, paving) done by crews; agent only produces proposals.
unit_economics_claims: Competitors typically take one to two days to respond

acquisition.how: Inbound lead response and proposal generation can be fully agent-run.

onboarding.how: Agent collects photos and job details.

billing.how: Invoicing automatable; quotes need human sign-off.

uk_applicability.notes: Works the same; UK satellite imagery available.

risks: AI visuals may overpromise vs actual work

quotes.text: We have a paving company that is using satellite imagery of uh large lots like parking lots that are clearly, you know, past their prime.
quotes.speaker: Alex

ideas.name: Pond dredging lead database
ideas.one_liner: Build a database of ponds needing dredging from satellite, GIS, tax and zoning data and sell leads to pond dredging/maintenance companies.
ideas.business_model: Sell lead lists or run pond dredging leads
ideas.customer: Pond dredging and maintenance companies; ranch/farm owners
ideas.problem: No directory of the roughly 800,000 Texas farm and ranch ponds exists
ideas.offer: Sheet of ponds with size, address and need signals
ideas.delivery: Agent sub-agents check satellite data and zoning applications in parallel and produce a leads webpage.
unit_economics_claims: Claude claimed about 800,000 ponds on Texas farms and ranches (unverified)

acquisition.how: Selling lead lists to companies needs outreach; limited-company cold email is legal.

delivery.how: Agent compiles lead data; accuracy needs checks.

support.how: Routine queries handled by an agent.

uk_applicability.notes: Texas ranch ponds are US-specific; UK analogue (farm ponds, lakes) is much smaller and data sources differ.

quotes.text: I said, is there a directory? Is there a place where I could sort through that? It's like, no, that's not a thing.
quotes.speaker: Chris Koerner

ideas.name: Sell niche AI agents to clients (AI automation agency on Hyper Agent)
ideas.one_liner: AI agencies build a niche agent (e.g. pond dredging project manager) and stamp it out per client in separate workspaces, with clients paying the AI costs.
ideas.business_model: Agency setup and management fees; client pays platform AI usage
ideas.customer: Small niche businesses; AI implementation agencies
ideas.problem: Agencies hack together private servers and struggle to package, deploy and bill agents
ideas.offer: Templated, niche-specific agents managed by the agency in per-client workspaces
ideas.delivery: Agency configures and edits agents; clients use them as end users.

acquisition.how: Outbound to limited companies only; needs human sales.

quotes.text: that becomes your template that you then stamp out across all your clients.
quotes.speaker: Alex

ideas.delivery: Agent logs into Facebook account and checks hourly, notifying via email, WhatsApp, Telegram, Slack.

delivery.how: Map generation is automated; the underlying laundromat business is physical.

quotes.text: Interactive map with 78 laundromats and four screening gap areas, overlapping searches, and then it even has a design here.

tactics.name: Agent-built website as outreach hook
steps: Prompt the agent to find local businesses with strong reviews but no or outdated website
Agent gathers contact info and learns brand from reviews
Agent builds a bespoke site and drafts a personalised email
Offer to implement within days, or give it free to open the conversation
Human approves emails, or trusts the agent to send

quote.text: here is an example of the type of website we'd be able to stand up for you within days.
quote.speaker: Alex

tactics.name: Personalised landing page per prospect
steps: Define ICP
Agent researches the specific project lead
Build a personal landing page with hero video, screenshots and a CTA to a study or pilot
Send it instead of a plain cold email
Review which messaging earns replies and feed learnings back

tactics.name: Persistent 'live mode' agent with permission separation
steps: Describe the job like a job description
Let the agent write its own loop prompt
Schedule it hourly
Have it post updates to Slack or Telegram
Separate agents for brand posting versus customer/financial data to enforce guardrails

quote.text: I can create hard guard rails by assigning those permissions to different agents.
quote.speaker: Alex

tactics.name: Instant visual response to inbound leads
steps: Agent replies to inbound leads immediately
Generate an image of the finished result from the customer's photo
Send with an estimate before competitors respond

tactics.name: Save research as a scheduled agent
steps: Run the research prompt
Click save as agent and name it
Add an invocation schedule in plain English with specifics (e.g. every morning 7am, new laundromats in other zip codes)

tools_mentioned.purpose: Persistent AI agent platform with browser, sub-agents, live mode and marketplace

tools_mentioned.name: Claude
tools_mentioned.purpose: Used for research and to prepare criteria files

warnings.warning: Agent output needs iteration: the motion design agent typically needs three or four rounds of feedback to meet a high standard.

quote.text: I expect to have to probably give it three or four rounds of feedback
quote.speaker: Alex

warnings.warning: Broker-reported earnings are unaudited; the AI flagged strong claims as unverified.
Keep customer/financial data agents separate from public-posting agents to avoid data crossing.
Reaching $500k owner profit usually requires multi-crew or multi-location scale.

lessons.lesson: Treat agents as persistent employees with a job description, narrow permissions and scheduled runs rather than one-off prompts.

quote.text: the metaphor is less about, oh, what are like chores and tedious things that I don't want to do?
quote.speaker: Alex

lessons.lesson: Personalised, visual deliverables (a built site, a mock-up) beat generic cold outreach because they show effort and let buyers self-serve asynchronously.
Fast response to inbound leads is a competitive advantage in local services.
Start with a tedious computer task you already do and ask an agent to build a dedicated agent for it.

quote.text: pick a part of your work that you find very tedious that you would like to not do anymore
quote.speaker: Alex

lessons.lesson: Agencies can package a niche agent as a template and deploy it per client in separate workspaces.
Have agents prompt humans (reports, approvals) rather than humans prompting agents.
Use the 'seller's discretionary earnings' view, not profit, when judging what a small business pays its owner.
Treat AI-generated income figures skeptically; verify with primary sources.

evidence_quality.rationale: Product demo by a vendor employee with no revenue or conversion data; anecdotal customer stories; AI-generated research figures unverified. Useful as a capability illustration only.
evidence_quality.promotional_conflict: Alex works for Hyper Agent and Chris promotes it with a referral/credits link; likely sponsored.
